title: Landing in Frankfurt to find no contract, and the American Consulate
summary: Arriving with seven dollars, Bubbles finds the producers had no contract signed, refuses to entertain soldiers for Bouveau, and gets the consulate to make Bouveau pay for his hotel.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So I got on the plane to go over there with about seven dollars in my pocket. Don't forget, all expenses paid. I could go a week without any money. They're going to take care of the hotel and everything. So what I got to worry about? That plane arrived in Frankfurt, Germany, the outskirts of Frankfurt. There was a phone call came into the airport to tell me to come to the airline office in Frankfurt. Well, I get a cab and the cab takes me to the airline office in Frankfurt. And I'm sitting in the cab, when I'm front of the door of American Airlines and looking at coming out the door was these two fellas. One light and one dark. And I say to myself, this can't be. Coming right towards the cab now. This can't be him. And it was him.

When he said to me, "How did you enjoy your trip," I knew that was him. "Oh, it was all right. He said, "Come on, we'll have some coffee and I'll call up the studio." He goes in to have coffee and I'm sitting down having the
coffee. While I'm sitting down having the coffee he's going to the phone booth which is --

... there was nothing left for us to do but to get somebody else, since you didn't sign the contract. So he came out of the phone booth, handed me the phone, let me talk to them let them know I was here. So I got on the phone, I says, "Hello, this is John Bubbles." "Yes?" "I understand I didn't sign the contract to let you know I was going to be here, huh?" "Well it ain't your fault. Okay, thank you, have a good day. Bye Bye." And I come out of the booth and I started to talk to him. He says, "He's crazy." I says, "She ain't crazy, she knows what she's saying. She did just what anybody else would have done. And you had me come this distance and you had no contract. How would you do a thing like that? Now, what are you saying now? Nothing you can say now but one thing. I've got to go back to America. He started to skip over the whole thing, you know. He don't think it's his fault at all. Here I am with seven dollars in my

pocket in Germany, can't speak German, can't sing German, can't do nothing in German. There was a band playing in Frankfurt, I knew the band and the band knew me -- understand? In the city, right next to where the airline office was is a cafe -- can't think of the name of the cafe. But anyway it's there, it's got American entertainment in there and he called me about getting some other work for me for the soldiers. And I says, no, I don't want to entertain the soldiers. I didn't want him to put me on nothing. I'm through with him now, you know. I can't kill him, I can't cut his throat, I can't do nothing but leave him alone. Can't even beat him up. So I just say, no, I don't want to entertain the soldiers to him. He calls up the head man of the western entertainment division and tells him about me not wanting to entertain the soldiers. That puts me in bad on the American too. So I -- he puts me in the Hauserzuhoff Hotel, Now I can't get out of the hotel unless I pay

the rent. So my next move is to go to the American Consulate. That's where I went and the American Consulate was the one that had him on the mat and told him what he had to do. He had to pay the hotel bill and get me a place to stay and take care of my expenses until I got back and get me back to America. Now he can't book me because I won't work for him.

So what did I do? I let him pay the hotel bill and get me out of the hotel and get me another place to stay. That's what he did. I still got thumbs down on him. You know that, you know. Here I am in Germany, can't do nothing.
